[[File:Building screenshot.jpg|thumb|A player building a house]] {{Quote|Raise your own viking mead halls, houses, castles, and more with our powerful construction interface. From knarrs to imposing warships, build legendary vessels to conquer the seas and discover new lands.https://www.valheimgame.com/home/#anchor2}} Valheim features an extensive '''building''' system that can be utilized to design structures to meet the demands of any discriminating warrior. In addition to humble homes and outposts, players also use this building interface to make enormous bases, elaborate works of art, defenses against the [[Creatures]] of Valheim, and unique tools to aid in their survival. Starting out with simple wooden building components, players will eventually gain access to the ability to create stronger structures with various materials, including stone and metal. == Basics == You can build using a [[Hammer]] within the working area of a [[Workbench]]. * Press [1-8] to select the hammer in the hotbar slot * Press [RMB] to open the build menu * Press [Q/E] to switch [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] category * Press [LMB] to chose [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]], and place it * Press [Middle Mouse Button] to remove [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Scroll the mouse to rotate the [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Hold [Shift] to temporarily disable snapping * Hold [Shift] then [Middle Mouse Button] to select [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you are looking at. There are various crafting stations required to be nearby to place certain [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. These include the following: * The [[Workbench]], required to place most [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you have unlocked from the beginning or early on, and some late [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. The Workbench is immediately available and costs 10 ordinary wood to build. * The [[Forge]], required to place most building parts containing metals. The Forge requires [[copper]] to build, and becomes available once the player can mine and refine [[Copper Ore]]. * The [[Stonecutter]], required to place building parts created out of stone, such as the stone walls some abandoned buildings are made out of. The Stonecutter requires [[iron]] to build, and becomes available once the player can collect and refine [[Scrap Iron]]. * The [[Artisan Table]], required to build some crafting stations that as of Patch 0.142.6 are at the end of implemented progression. The Artisan Table requires [[Dragon Tear|Dragon Tears]] to build, which must be obtained by defeating the fourth boss, [[Moder]] the dragon. == Snap building == Most building components can snap to each other. This allows for quick and easy building, but can be temporarily disabled by holding the appropriate key or button. By default, this is L-Shift on mouse and keyboard, and LT+LB on controller. == Structural integrity == {{Main|Building stability}} If there is not enough support, the building pieces will fall down. You may reinforce the building with walls, beams, and poles. When you move the cursor to the building piece, it shows a color range from blue, to green, to red. Blue indicates that the part is as stable as it can be, as dictated by its material. The closer to red on the spectrum, the less stable the part. Attempting to place additional pieces onto one that is fully red may result in the new part breaking off and dropping the resources used to construct it unless the new part has lower stability requirements. The stability of an individual building piece is determined by its material, the stability of the piece it's anchored to and its position relative to it, each additional piece inheriting a fraction of the previous piece's stability. A directly vertical pole of [[Wood]] or [[Stone]] can rise 16 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Wood Wall]], [[Wood Wall Half]], [[Stone Wall 1x1]], [[Stone Wall 2x1]], [[Stone Wall 4x2]], [[Wood Pole 1 m]], [[Wood Pole 2 m]], [[Stone Pillar]]. A directly vertical pole of [[Corewood]] Logs can rise 24 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Log Pole 4 m]] and [[Log Pole 2 m]]. A directly vertical [[Wood Iron Pole]] can rise up to 50 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. Trees, including those planted by the player, will effectively function as "the ground" for support purposes, allowing for extremely high construction. [[File:Structure integrity.png|thumb|Found on [https://www.reddit.com/r/valheim/comments/lqsxki/updated_psa_structural_support_details/ Reddit /Valheim], thanks to [https://www.reddit.com/user/ToddGeorgeKelly/ user/ToddGeorgeKelly/]]] In order to keep tall structures stable, the tallest point should be reinforced by supports that create the shortest and most vertical path possible down to the ground. It is worth considering raising the terrain as much as possible below a structure, such that the floor and walls are 100% stable (highlighted in blue when moused over). Boulders are also considered terrain when calculating stability, so parts that intersect them are considered grounded. == Decay == If wooden building sections are not covered during rain, are not linked to a roof, or are submerged in water, they will decay to a maximum of 50% durability and will seem rotting until fixed. When exposed to rain, defensive structures do not rot decay. Stone, black marble, and crystal structures will not decay when wet or submerged. Building the desired structure's roof first, with the appropriate supports and foundation in place, will aid with constructions lasting days or weeks if rain is a worry. == Damage == Player, monster, and creature attacks can all damage structures. Defensive structures will also receive minor damage while causing harm to creatures that come into contact with them. Aggressive creatures are drawn to and hostile toward all light sources (excluding Jack-o-turnips) and crafting stations, and will try to break them if not attacking a player. == Repair == You can repair building parts that seem to be decaying or damaged with a [[Hammer]]. This does not cost any resources, but does consume stamina. The player must be in range of a crafting station that corresponds to the part being repaired, e.g. a [[Workbench]] when repairing a wooden part, or a [[Stonecutter]] for a stone part. == Abandoned buildings == These structures are a type of [[point of interest]] that can be found to naturally occur in the world. The size, layout, and materials these structures are made of can vary greatly as each is generated from random templates. There are different types of abandoned structures such as Abandoned Cabins, Abandoned Towers, Abandoned Farms just to name a few. These abandoned and generated structures can contain things such as chests with items specific to the biome, monsters (usually [[Skeleton]]s), [[:Category:Creature spawner|monster spawner]]s, and [[wikipedia:Vegvísir|Vegvisir]]s to mark the nearest boss altar for that biome. In the Meadows/Black Forest biome, they can also contain naturally spawning [[Beehive]]s, which will drop a [[Queen Bee]] and sometimes [[Honey]] when destroyed. Players should approach abandoned villages with caution since some villages have been reoccupied by [[Draugr]] and [[Draugr Elite]] who will attack the player on sight. These [[Draugr village|Draugr Villages]] can be identified by partial walls of sharp logs and the buzzing of the [[Creature spawner|spawners]] inside several of the buildings as well as a general miasma and the presence of Draugr both inside and outside the structures. They almost always have a large Mead Hall building that cannot be found anywhere else. There may also be a sentry in a tower armed with a bow who will snipe anything that comes near. == Player base and blocking spawning == {{Main|Player base}} Building certain structures considered to be 'player base' will have the following effects in a radius around them: * Prevent [[creatures|creature]] spawning * Prevent items dropped on the ground from despawning after 1 hour (unless submerged) * Enable player base [[events]] to occur For a full list of player base structures, see [[player base]]. == Base building strategies == [[File:Mordheim server - Guild Castle.jpg|thumb|850x850px]] * Building your outposts in close proximity to '''several biome borders''' grants access to varied resources and allows you to observe the territorial in-fighting of different creatures (complete with loot strewn across the terrain), but can also be dangerous. * Many types of '''defenses''' are possible, both in the form of built objects and altered terrain: ** Creatures cannot dig through terrain, making '''"terrain walls" effectively impenetrable''' to them. Thus the perfect defense is built either with a hoe and a pile of rocks, any pickaxe or ideally a combination of the two. Be warned that terrain alterations may cause stutter just as placing objects does (press F2 to check the number of "instances" loaded). ** A hoe can be used to raise terrain while you're standing on it, allowing you to quickly erect a '''pillar''' to stand on and shoot melee enemies below. Beware that you need a workbench nearby to do this. With practice this is possible during combat. ** Most creatures never jump down from ledges (Fenring and Blobs are exceptions). A '''deep pit''' (around 3 "blocks") is also largely safe, and you can shoot enemies coming close to the ledge. Flying creatures may attack from above if you don't build a roof, however. ** Gates can be destroyed, but '''gaps''' the player jumps over when entering or exiting the base cannot. This trick can be inconvenient, however. Also note that you can '''scale steep terrain''' walls by sprinting and jump-spamming, especially when moving towards a crease (corner) for better traction, while most creatures cannot. ** The most '''FPS-efficient method of defense''' is to build on a few terrain pillars. This minimizes terrain alteration "instances" yet allows you to ignore enemies running around outside, especially if the base entrance requires a quick hop to get on. Note that returning terrain to its roughly native height doesn't remove the FPS hit (unless a true "undo terrain changes" tool is added to the game). ** Workbenches (and campfires) '''disallow enemy spawns''' in their radius, making them surprisingly useful defensive tools. You can hide these in the outer perimeter of your walls or in small pits covered with a few floor tiles to make an area safer. Workbenches also stop dropped items from de-spawning over time, however. ** Doors and gates can be used to create a '''toggle-able bridge''' for carts. Another option to defend your bridge is to hang a gate from a support above it and attach the floor piece to the gate with small gaps on the sides, causing the floor to disappear if the gate is destroyed. ** You can place '''gates in the water''' to block enemies, who will be unable to attack the gates, yet allow boats to pass when opened. * The '''"Level Ground"''' option for the hoe uses the terrain height directly underneath you as the target altitude, though if you hold Shift while clicking it'll use the altitude of the terrain you're pointing at instead. Using this knowledge well may save you a lot of stone and work while landscaping as it only expends stamina and hoe durability. * You can also build a '''"gangplank"''' for enemies to walk on, above your pit base, and put a campfire on it so they'll kill themselves, then catch the loot when it drops down. * Combining a moat with a plateau-based outpost is an interesting option. At some point in time, he set up camp within the Black Forest and tamed a [[Lox]] named [[Halstein]] that can be seen feeding from a bowl in the same camp. Haldor is a Dvergr or "dwarf", according to his introduction on Iron Gate's bloghttps://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-713.0-713.40, and how he refers to himself by one of his many quotes. This can happen from 320 to 453 meters away (about twice of the default minimap range) when the related [[Zones]] are generated. When discovered, his bag icon will appear on the world map. '''Yggdrasil''', also called the '''World-Tree''', is an immense sacred tree visible in the sky above ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''.

== Description ==
The World-Tree appears as a gigantic set of colorful branches that curves around the entire world of ''Valheim''. The titanic branches visibly pulsate with a strange greenish-blue resin and have various areas of vegetation adorning them. The core of the branches curves around the world and disappears into the horizon.

The enormous array of glowing branches that can be seen very high in the sky during clear weather is a part of the World-Tree. According to the [[lore]], this tree was once anchored to ''Valheim'', as well as nine other worlds, before [[Odin]] severed the boughs that connected ''Valheim'' to it after designating the world as a prison for his [[Creatures|foes]].

Parts of Yggdrasil can be found and accessed in [[Mistlands]] as [[Yggdrasil Shoot]]s, the source of {{Item link|Yggdrasil Wood}}, and [[Ancient Roots]], the source of {{Item link|Sap}}.

== Notes ==
* In Norse cosmology, the Yggdrasil is an immense and central sacred tree. All of existence resides around Yggdrasil, as well as the Nine Worlds which are connected directly to the tree.
* The name Yggdrasil is not designated to the World-Tree in any of the in-game lore. However, game assets do refer to this tree as Yggdrasil. It can be reasonably assumed that the World-Tree is the Yggdrasil of Norse lore.
* Using console commands, the player can float upwards and reach the branches of the World-Tree. Currently, the branches are incorporeal and the player character will fly right through them.
* The various "twigs" that are patched across the branches are roughly the size of regular trees in the world.

[[File:Crafting screenshot.png|thumb|A group of players using crafting stations]]
'''Crafting''' is the process of converting and combining [[materials]] to create new [[items]]. 

Some basic items can be crafted in the player inventory, but most items require a dedicated crafting station such as a [[Workbench]] or [[Forge]]. Most gear can also be upgraded to a higher quality, increasing its durability and other aspects.

== Crafting mechanics ==
[[File:Crafting-a-Cultivator.jpg|thumb|The crafting interface of a level 2 Forge, showing the recipe of a [[Cultivator]]. The station level is shown within the star in the top right. The craft tab allows crafting new items, whereas the upgrade tab allows upgrading gear currently in the inventory.]]

Crafting an item at a crafting station requires having the appropriate materials in the [[inventory]], as well as an available slot in the inventory for the result.

Gear that has durability can be repaired for free using the hammer icon at the side of the crafting interface at the crafting station where it was crafted (excluding the inventory). Gear that requires a higher station level to be crafed can also only be repaired at a station at that level, upgrading it does not increase this requirement.

Most weapons, tools and armors can be upgraded to higher qualities, often up to 3 times to a quality of 4. Each upgrade level requires a higher station level. Upgrading increases the durability of the item, and also improves its properties: weapons deal higher damage, while armors provide more [[Armor]]. Upgrading costs a considerable amount of resources and can double or triple the crafting cost of a given item over its cost at quality 1.

For example, the [[Troll Leather Tunic]] requires a level 2 Workbench to be crafted. Thus, it cannot be repaired at a level 1 Workbench. Upgrading it to quality 2 requires a level 3 Workbench, to quality 3 a level 4 Workbench, etc. It initially costs 6 [[Troll Hide]] to craft, but upgrading it to quality 4 costs an additional 11 Troll Hide for a total of 17.

[[Hugin]] | marital = | birthDate = | birthPlace = | deathDate = | deathPlace = | species = Bird | gender = Male | height = | weight = | eyes = Pale yellow }} '''Munin''' is a [[Creatures#NPCs|character]] found in ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. He is a large, talking raven who provides guidance to slain Vikings that have newly arrived in the [[Mistlands]], along with [[Hugin]]. ==Biography== Nothing is known about Munin beyond the fact that he is a large, male raven with the ability to speak and spontaneously appear and disappear wherever he pleases. In [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_mythology Norse mythology], Munin is one of the two named ravens along with Hugin that were used to bring information to the god [[Odin]]. It is unclear, however, if Munin serves the same purpose within ''[[Valheim]]''.{{Tocright}} ==Tutorial== As new milestones in the [[Mistlands]] are achieved, Munin will appear and offer useful information. He will continue to reappear next to the player until the player interacts with him to read his message. {| class="wikitable" ! Introduction |- |Kraa! Well met, wanderer… I am Munin, brother to Hugin. I bring greetings from the Allfather. His eye sees through mine, I carry his words beneath my tongue. Keep his ways and I will come to you again… |- ! [[Giant Remains]] |- |Shadows of an ancient age. The Jotunn once ruled the tenth world, until their time ran out and they were ousted by some other power. |- ! Dvergr |- |Take care, warrior. You've happened upon an outpost of the forlorn Dvergr clans, long since separated from their kin in Nidavellir. Trapped here they still toil, expecting reprieve that will never come. It is a sad fate... |- ! [[Infested Mine]] |- |These are the Dvergrhomes, built long ago in a gilded age... Their splendour rivalled the Golden Hall itself! Regrettably, nothing can last forever.
